approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves scored molecular graphs with crossover and mutation, draws breeding parents from high-scoring bands of its current survivor population, and keeps a full archive of accepted scores. Before each new proposal batch, a Gaussian process fits every accepted record using local molecular count fingerprints. It evaluates a fresh pool of offspring through correlated sampled functions and selects their available maxima. Real offspring scores update both this predictor and the score-greedy breeding population. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled, while continuation, crossover finishing mutation, stable identity admission and bounded numerical fallbacks remain active.
approach.novelty: Control the ongoing-learning path by fitting the same active Gaussian process only to immutable copies of the original usable initial observations at every suggestion. Its initial training membership, labels and normalization stay fixed together. Later accepted scores still enter the full archive and determine live survivors and breeding parents. This differs from removing predictive selection or fixing breeding parents: current offspring still receive correlated GP predictions and evaluation choices, but generated labels cannot teach that predictor. The experiment asks what this one feedback path contributes, rather than proposing that a static predictor is a better optimizer.

hypothesis: Freeze the active count-Tanimoto GP training dataset to immutable copies of the original usable initial accepted archive in its original order for every inherited fit, jointly freezing its empirical label normalization while retaining full real-archive feedback for live graph breeding and the original correlated posterior allocation on fresh pools.

finding_summary.headline: Continued GP conditioning contributes: initial-only training lowers every matched endpoint and the mean by 0.151856.
finding_summary.insights:
Ongoing conditioning on generated accepted observations adds value beyond an initially fitted predictor in this optimizer, even when real-label survival, recursive breeding and posterior selection remain active. The experiment therefore answers a narrower question than removing the whole selector or freezing the breeding cohort. Training membership, later label information and empirical normalization were held together: their individual effects, and their interaction with survival, remain unassigned. All sitagliptin fits retain the initial scale floor, but this exposure alone does not establish that the floor causes its endpoint losses.

Useful local search persists under the frozen predictor. It produces 580 best-parent wins and 125 incumbent advances, and every endpoint exceeds its initial best. The molecular assessment finds recognizable amide and aromatic-carbonyl families, useful available amines, changed linkers and ring closures. Some lower-scoring Child leaders have more conventional local chemistry than their Parent counterparts; other outputs retain reactive bonds, doubtful ring geometry and unresolved stereochemistry. The loss does not establish absent chemical novelty, require reactive motifs or identify a chemical mediator. Three leaders arrive in the final batch and cannot show later feedback effects.

The lower selected-stream prediction error is measured on different molecules and cannot establish better calibration or replace the endpoint contrast. Likewise, passive full-archive calculations change all 420 later selected sets on the actual Child pools, but do not supply alternative rewards or future histories. This complete exposed result ends the registered initial-cohort control. Shared-Parent sibling experiments and historical repeated trajectories are dependent evidence, so their effects cannot be added or treated as independent replications.
finding_summary.results:
All 435 GP fits keep the same ten initial accepted molecules, raw labels and normalization within each task/seed. Across 420 later fits, 4,200 generated observations remain in the real archive but never enter training; the 150 final observations have no later fit opportunity. Predictions for the same previously emitted molecule stay fixed to numerical precision. The selector remains active on every fresh 160-member pool, with nonzero correlated draws. Recursive breeding also remains active: 1,751 accepted offspring later serve as parents in 102,673 draws.

Every first batch matches the Parent. In batch two, the same pool and normal draws produce different evaluated sets after the first excluded feedback; parent and pool histories diverge in batch three. All three replicas complete. Mean final Top-1 falls from 0.595670 to 0.443813, a paired change of -0.151856 against the predicted loss scale of 0.002. Seed changes are -0.181637, -0.118363 and -0.155569. All fifteen endpoints and all five task means decline. The zaleplon result in seed zero nearly matches its Parent, losing only 0.000484, while the largest loss is 0.430456 in docking seed two. Seed dispersion also falls, around the lower mean.

molecular.headline: Familiar aromatic amides and carbonyl heterocycles persist, with useful amines but incomplete context control and reactive ring chemistry
molecular.overall_character: All supplied Child n-7de8feaf821f and published Parent n-62daf219c70a trajectories were present and read. The brief independently reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true for Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, with no profile mismatch or uncovered objective. Each task contributes 900 Child records, including 870 optimizer evaluations; all matched task/seed initial molecule and score records agree. Every Child retained best exceeds its fixed initial best, while all fifteen matched Parent endpoints remain higher. The seed-0 indole-amide comparison is nearly matched, whereas several available-amine and fluorinated-heterocycle comparisons differ substantially. The Child produces recurrent indole carboxamides, aryl-linked nitrogen/carbonyl systems, amide and sulfonamide material with available amines, and bridged or fused nitrogen rings. Many recognizable initial functional-group arrangements remain visible in leading output, but actual recursive breeding also produces changed linkers, new ring closures and useful simplifications. There is moderate chemical diversity across families and seeds, with narrower useful leading neighborhoods; this is not global structural collapse or an inability to produce rings. In fixed task order the digest ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9931, 0.9471, 0.969, 0.9828 and 0.954, and aromatic-string incidences are 0.9931, 0.9425, 0.9575, 0.9586 and 0.9241. These are text-feature incidences, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 throughout. The respective cross-seed distinct-identity counts are 841, 870, 876, 874 and 870; each task/seed still has 300 distinct accepted identities. Cross-seed recurrence is not within-run duplicate evaluation. The moderate drug-likeness reading reflects familiar amides, ethers, carbonyl heterocycles and available amines in many leaders. It does not imply confirmed activity or easy synthesis. Synthetic plausibility remains questionable because other accepted molecules carry N-F or O-Cl bonds, peroxide/peracid groups, unusual imines and four-membered or bridged closures, and because very large joined products recur. Several conventional Child indole-amide and amine leaders avoid reactive bonds found in their Parent counterparts, so lower observed scores do not uniformly mean worse chemical plausibility. Read-only RDKit descriptors were calculated from the supplied trajectories; no objective, affinity or synthesis score was generated. The authorized source and receipts distinguish the immutable original usable accepted GP cohort from the complete real observation archive and the live score-ranked breeding population. Across the recorded Child fits, the initial ten training records and their label mean/scale remain the training basis, while final real archives contain all 300 accepted records. The later accepted leaders have genuine raw scores, enter the real archive and survive by the inherited score law; their absence from GP training is not rejection or loss of genetic feedback. For example, the seed-0 amine/amide leader appears in the next context as a live rank-0 survivor and archived observation but not a training member, and later actually breeds a high-scoring accepted analogue. The same distinction holds for a leading pyridyl indole amide whose later accepted descendant loses useful context and scores poorly. These are molecular provenance examples, not an activation verdict. The full-pool receipts retain the inherited pool size, and current molecules still receive current predictions and correlated selection draws. A fixed training cohort does not mean constant predictions for different molecules, frozen pools, static initial breeders or removal of the selector. The inherited archive_mean prediction field is explicitly scoped in these receipts to the initial training mean; its name does not make it the current complete-archive mean. Training membership, later-label information and empirical normalization are held together in this control; their separate effects, whole-selector contribution and whole-foundation contribution are not identified here. All thirty Child/Parent task/seed leaders were joined to actual pooled, emitted and accepted records and their generating scored parents. Initial-source molecules, unscored graph intermediates, pooled offspring, emitted proposals, accepted observations, live survivors, actual breeders and retained-best endpoints remain distinct. Some late leaders have no later feedback opportunity; another recorded leader breeds a chlorinated pooled analogue with no accepted label. No score or chemical benefit is imputed to that unqueried molecule. Chemical frequencies and missing-feature statements concern accepted trajectories and leaders, not a census of the full unselected pool. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 observations, not all seeds' retained best. The original gap reports in n-c55c3d520a2c and their identical-trajectory carry-forward in n-62daf219c70a were read through the fresh legal evidence index. Historical reproduction is provenance, not independent replication. This single complete matched panel shares a Parent baseline with other current routes and has adaptive histories; no independent-replication, combined, additive or interaction claim follows. Chemical association and overlapping ancestry do not establish mediation or separate predictive from survival contributions. All supplied source, trajectory and log paths were present. Audits under .slots/r0020-03-ablation-L01/molecular/ preserve trajectory descriptors, source/log hashes, leader_training_provenance.json, original gap provenance and citation joins. Only Child digest/trusted-trajectory SMILES are quoted; Parent-only molecules are identified by their published task, seed and evaluation.

per_task.generated_character: Accepted offspring have median 25 heavy atoms and three perceived rings, with the leading structures retaining an NH-indole carboxamide linked to a fluoroaniline or pyridyl ring. The seed-0 leader at evaluation 272 has 24 heavy atoms, methoxy/methyl substitution and a mercaptomethyl group; seed 1/evaluation 101 has 24 heavy atoms and a vinyl ether, methoxy and pyridyl amide; seed 2/evaluation 145 has 23 heavy atoms with methoxy and two methyl groups. All three are recognizable compact aromatic amides without N-halogen bonds or carbon cumulenes. The vinyl ether and free thiol still pose local stability questions, but these leaders are more conventional than many Parent leaders. The Parent endpoints at seed 0/evaluation 289, seed 1/evaluation 293 and seed 2/evaluation 294 instead include an N-chloroindole cumulene, an N-fluoro/N-hydroxy pyridyl amide and an N-chloroindole aryl diketone. The complete Child stream also contains doubled indole assemblies, reactive halogen/peroxide derivatives and fragments; its conventional leaders do not describe every evaluated molecule.
liabilities: Vinyl ether and free-thiol substitution in two leaders requires stability scrutiny; other accepted derivatives introduce N-halogen, O-halogen or peroxide connections.
Joined bis-indole products reach 49 heavy atoms and extremely low observed scores, while small late derivatives can lose the beneficial pendant aromatic/amide context.
missing_features: The useful compact aromatic-amide organization is present, but the evaluated leading family offers few comparably useful alternatives beyond peripheral substituent changes; the stronger Parent polar-group arrangements are not consistently reached.

There is no demonstrated need for the Parent leaders' N-halogen or cumulene motifs: a conventional Child amide nearly matches one Parent endpoint, while other families remain below their matched endpoints.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and is retained through the identical published chemistry of n-62daf219c70a; historical reproduction is not independent replication. Current evidence is n-7de8feaf821f versus n-62daf219c70a on complete matched Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per objective, batch size 10 and the frozen Research-in-Depth epoch-1 profile. The current control holds the original usable initial GP cohort, labels and empirical mean/scale together while keeping the complete real accepted archive, raw-label genetic survival/rank breeding, recursion and full correlated full-pool selector active. Evidence describes accepted chemistry and inspected provenance, not rewards or absence of chemistry in unselected pools, separate normalization effects or whole-selector/foundation contribution. Leading products retain indole carboxamides, aromatic nitrogen diones and amide/sulfonamide-rich aryl systems; within a seed, many useful changes are peripheral substitutions. Different seeds nevertheless reach distinct ring and linker families, useful deletions and available-amine products. Every Child retained best improves on its initial best. A conventional compact amide nearly matches one Parent endpoint, while the complete panel leaves other stronger Parent arrangements unreached. This is uneven useful coverage, not absent novelty or absent recursive generation.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently provide useful alternatives beyond recurring inherited functional-group and scaffold combinations in evaluated output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Develop chemically coherent alternative arrangements under legal task-local feedback and assess their actual evaluated descendants, rather than treating identity counts or retained initial motifs as sufficient coverage. Real acceptance and genetic reuse must remain distinguishable from admission to a predictive training set. This molecular finding neither authorizes tuning the bounded training-cohort control nor isolates training membership, label information, normalization, survival or total optimizer effects.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

original_finding_summary.headline: The same-code baseline reproduces all trajectories and the 0.595670 mean
original_finding_summary.insights: The campaign now has a complete baseline under the opening Research in Depth profile, with the exchange-free implementation and its feedback chain verified. Repeating the same seeds reproduced the same search histories; this adds execution and profile-baseline evidence without adding independent search trajectories or isolating any retained component’s value. The earlier finding that removing direct exchanges improved the mean remains a historical counterexample to the predicted loss, and is not retested here. The chemistry also reproduces the earlier limits: useful aromatic/carbonyl and aryl-amine arrangements coexist with reactive heteroatom–halogen bonds, doubtful ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry. Those liabilities and uneven task dispersion persist at the reproduced score. Current-profile component interventions are still needed to determine which retained mechanisms support that score and whether useful chemistry can be preserved while improving reliability.
original_finding_summary.results: All fifteen task runs completed. Final Top-1 macro mean was 0.595670, with seed population SD 0.026593; the three seed macros were 0.625412, 0.560866 and 0.600731. Every endpoint and every molecular trajectory reproduced the historical Anchor. Direct exchanges remained absent despite 904 eligible selected-site menus with 1,276 withheld partners. Accepted-only learning, crossover and correlated posterior selection all executed. The 4,350 accepted offspring produced 629 best-parent beats, 258 incumbent improvements and 2,401 later-used breeding molecules, exactly as before. The historical seeds are all profile-mismatched, so the protocol provides no paired effect estimate.

original_finding_summary.headline: Generation-order allocation loses 0.124388 in mean endpoint score despite retaining full pool and model effort.
original_finding_summary.insights:
This closes a different question from the earlier count, residual and correlation controls: allocating evaluations using the complete predictive selector matters even when generation effort is held at the inherited full-pool boundary. The earlier selector addition also enlarged the pool and lacked a complete matched Parent panel, so it could not establish this conditional contrast. Local parent beats increased from 629 to 653, yet incumbent improvements fell from 258 to 163; adaptive local success is not a substitute for endpoint quality. The present loss does not apportion value among posterior means, counts, residual amplitude or correlation, and separate sibling losses cannot be added.

A plausible place to investigate the loss is how evaluation choices preserve useful chemical relationships across adaptive histories. The molecular report finds that generation-order output still reaches useful nitrile and aryl-amine alternatives, including both improved endpoints, while other streams move into densely connected heteroatom frameworks and miss strong Parent families. Reactive bonds, questionable ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry persist. This concerns the evaluated distribution; it does not show that better alternatives were absent from the complete pools or identify a chemical mediator. Passive alternatives have no counterfactual scores.

Removing predictive influence is also different from removing computational cost: all surplus generation and model computations remain, and numerical failures would still use the inherited routes. No reduced-pool, compute-saving or optimizer-deletion conclusion follows. Actual recovery branches remain unexercised despite passing deterministic synthetic checks.

All 435 successful batches evaluated the first ten members of a completed 160-member pool, with zero prefix-order violations or choices outside that prefix. The passive original sampler selected a different set in all 435 batches, and its sampled values strictly preferred another candidate on 4,317 of 4,350 generation-order masks. Thus the removal changed real evaluation choices under strong exposure. All 435 fits, full covariance factorizations and original normal arrays remained computed; the accepted-only feedback and identity-bound prediction joins passed. No natural numerical fallback or incomplete pool occurred.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.471282, a paired change of -0.124388, well beyond the registered 0.002 loss scale. Seed macro changes were -0.134968, -0.105769 and -0.132426. Macro population deviation changed from 0.026593 to 0.014583. Correct removal and the predicted score loss support positive contribution from the composite selector in this exact full-pool search loop.

original_finding_summary.headline: Recursive breeding feedback contributes: fixing initial parents lowers every matched endpoint and the mean by 0.260206.
original_finding_summary.insights:
These complete, exposed results establish positive conditional contribution of recursive offspring-to-breeder feedback within the current optimizer, even while accepted-label posterior learning remains active. The initial cohort contains ten molecules, but only five have positive support under the inherited unexcluded quantile law. Fixing that breeder holds membership, ordering and cohort size together; this experiment cannot apportion their effects or isolate the survivor rule. It also leaves the broader whole-foundation question open. Separate component removals and shared-Parent siblings cannot be added into a joint value estimate.

The local success counts illustrate why ancestry and endpoint quality must be kept separate. Beating an initial molecule becomes more common, and prediction errors are smaller on the changed evaluated distribution, yet the search makes fewer incumbent gains and ends lower. Every Child endpoint still exceeds its initial best. The molecular assessment finds useful available amines, ring closures and scaffold rearrangements alongside recurring initial amide, nitrile/carbonyl and dione organizations. Some lower-scoring Child leaders have more familiar local chemistry than the higher-scoring Parent leaders. The deficit therefore does not establish an absence of chemical novelty, require reactive motifs, or identify a chemical mediator. Scored ancestry depth one also allows unscored multistep edits and crossover finishing.

The fixed neighborhoods remained productive enough to fill all full pools under inherited bounds, although they required more attempts. No rescue from live survivors was used. Exhaustion and recovery semantics passed source and synthetic checks but were not naturally exercised. Three matched Search seeds support this descriptive conditional result; they do not establish universal reliability or value for unobserved descendants.

original_finding_summary.headline: Incumbent targeting raises sampled batch utility, but smaller real gains lower all three seed means
original_finding_summary.insights:
The experiment exposes a failure of the complete incumbent-referenced allocation rule under this Parent: correct positive-improvement targeting and higher sampled utility did not deliver larger real advances. More update events again accompanied smaller increments. The mean realized batch-improvement contrast telescopes to the final-score contrast on these equal-length streams, so those two failures should not be counted as independent endpoint evidence. The result supports a negative contribution from this whole rule under the tested composition. A threshold-only endpoint effect remains unresolved because the current unthresholded comparison has no separately evaluated future trajectory.

Finite-panel zero gain also failed to identify unproductive molecules. Fourteen zero-gain choices beat their frozen real incumbent, eleven made sequential incumbent updates, 205 were later bred and 119 survived to the final populations. Two became session leaders. Every one of those fourteen real wins had no sampled scenario above the incumbent. The chemical report includes a ring-free urea/enamide/thiocarbonyl leader and a distinct aza-dicarbonyl leader in this group. These are concrete limits of the sampled improvement support; they do not establish whether model error, finite tail sampling, myopic selection or later breeding caused the overall loss.

Selected-stream MSE and interval coverage improved while within-batch ordering weakened, but the selected molecules and histories changed. Those diagnostics do not establish repaired uncertainty or improved chemistry. Familiar amines and lactams still coexist with reactive bonds, difficult rings, large assemblies and unspecified stereochemistry. The older unthresholded and antithetic failures retain their exchange-containing Parent conditions, and shared-Parent siblings supply no isolated threshold, additive or joint-component effect. The complete exposed endpoint failure supplies the registered approach-review evidence without authorizing acquisition tuning.

original_finding_summary.headline: Atom-pair information changed search and split six local aliases, but the mean endpoint fell by 0.033408
original_finding_summary.insights: More descriptor distinctions and better predictions on selected molecules did not yield better endpoint search in this fixed mixture. On the actual accepted stream, raw MSE improved from 0.009475 for the passive local model to 0.009335, and mean batch ordering correlation rose from 0.545819 to 0.571243, despite the endpoint loss. These improvements were uneven: MSE worsened in seven task/seed cells, including all median_2 cells. Ordinary similarity and regularization changes were broadly exposed, whereas alias-mediated benefit was not: ten members of five split pool pairs remained unscored, and only one member of the cross pair was evaluated. Thirteen other pairs shared atom-pair counts but remained distinguishable through local counts; the channels still do not establish complete molecular identity. The negative result belongs to this one equal-weight composition and does not undo the earlier evidence for retaining local occurrence counts or isolate atom-pair information from mixture weighting. Molecular evidence still shows reactive heteroatom-halogen and sulfur motifs, large linked assemblies and destructive fragments alongside conventional high-scoring chemistry. Added topological information does not enforce chemical feasibility, and neither a universal size explanation nor an alias-resolution explanation is established.

original_finding_summary.headline: The same-code baseline reproduces all trajectories and the 0.595670 mean
original_finding_summary.insights: The campaign now has a complete baseline under the opening Research in Depth profile, with the exchange-free implementation and its feedback chain verified. Repeating the same seeds reproduced the same search histories; this adds execution and profile-baseline evidence without adding independent search trajectories or isolating any retained component’s value. The earlier finding that removing direct exchanges improved the mean remains a historical counterexample to the predicted loss, and is not retested here. The chemistry also reproduces the earlier limits: useful aromatic/carbonyl and aryl-amine arrangements coexist with reactive heteroatom–halogen bonds, doubtful ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry. Those liabilities and uneven task dispersion persist at the reproduced score. Current-profile component interventions are still needed to determine which retained mechanisms support that score and whether useful chemistry can be preserved while improving reliability.
original_finding_summary.results: All fifteen task runs completed. Final Top-1 macro mean was 0.595670, with seed population SD 0.026593; the three seed macros were 0.625412, 0.560866 and 0.600731. Every endpoint and every molecular trajectory reproduced the historical Anchor. Direct exchanges remained absent despite 904 eligible selected-site menus with 1,276 withheld partners. Accepted-only learning, crossover and correlated posterior selection all executed. The 4,350 accepted offspring produced 629 best-parent beats, 258 incumbent improvements and 2,401 later-used breeding molecules, exactly as before. The historical seeds are all profile-mismatched, so the protocol provides no paired effect estimate.

original_finding_summary.headline: Generation-order allocation loses 0.124388 in mean endpoint score despite retaining full pool and model effort.
original_finding_summary.insights:
This closes a different question from the earlier count, residual and correlation controls: allocating evaluations using the complete predictive selector matters even when generation effort is held at the inherited full-pool boundary. The earlier selector addition also enlarged the pool and lacked a complete matched Parent panel, so it could not establish this conditional contrast. Local parent beats increased from 629 to 653, yet incumbent improvements fell from 258 to 163; adaptive local success is not a substitute for endpoint quality. The present loss does not apportion value among posterior means, counts, residual amplitude or correlation, and separate sibling losses cannot be added.

A plausible place to investigate the loss is how evaluation choices preserve useful chemical relationships across adaptive histories. The molecular report finds that generation-order output still reaches useful nitrile and aryl-amine alternatives, including both improved endpoints, while other streams move into densely connected heteroatom frameworks and miss strong Parent families. Reactive bonds, questionable ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry persist. This concerns the evaluated distribution; it does not show that better alternatives were absent from the complete pools or identify a chemical mediator. Passive alternatives have no counterfactual scores.

Removing predictive influence is also different from removing computational cost: all surplus generation and model computations remain, and numerical failures would still use the inherited routes. No reduced-pool, compute-saving or optimizer-deletion conclusion follows. Actual recovery branches remain unexercised despite passing deterministic synthetic checks.
original_finding_summary.results:
All 435 successful batches evaluated the first ten members of a completed 160-member pool, with zero prefix-order violations or choices outside that prefix. The passive original sampler selected a different set in all 435 batches, and its sampled values strictly preferred another candidate on 4,317 of 4,350 generation-order masks. Thus the removal changed real evaluation choices under strong exposure. All 435 fits, full covariance factorizations and original normal arrays remained computed; the accepted-only feedback and identity-bound prediction joins passed. No natural numerical fallback or incomplete pool occurred.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.471282, a paired change of -0.124388, well beyond the registered 0.002 loss scale. Seed macro changes were -0.134968, -0.105769 and -0.132426. Correct removal and the predicted score loss support positive contribution from the composite selector in this exact full-pool search loop.

original_finding_summary.headline: Recursive breeding feedback contributes: fixing initial parents lowers every matched endpoint and the mean by 0.260206.
original_finding_summary.insights:
These complete, exposed results establish positive conditional contribution of recursive offspring-to-breeder feedback within the current optimizer, even while accepted-label posterior learning remains active. The initial cohort contains ten molecules, but only five have positive support under the inherited unexcluded quantile law. Fixing that breeder holds membership, ordering and cohort size together; this experiment cannot apportion their effects or isolate the survivor rule. It also leaves the broader whole-foundation question open. Separate component removals and shared-Parent siblings cannot be added into a joint value estimate.

The local success counts illustrate why ancestry and endpoint quality must be kept separate. Beating an initial molecule becomes more common, and prediction errors are smaller on the changed evaluated distribution, yet the search makes fewer incumbent gains and ends lower. Every Child endpoint still exceeds its initial best. The molecular assessment finds useful available amines, ring closures and scaffold rearrangements alongside recurring initial amide, nitrile/carbonyl and dione organizations. Some lower-scoring Child leaders have more familiar local chemistry than the higher-scoring Parent leaders. The deficit therefore does not establish an absence of chemical novelty, require reactive motifs, or identify a chemical mediator. Scored ancestry depth one also allows unscored multistep edits and crossover finishing.

The fixed neighborhoods remained productive enough to fill all full pools under inherited bounds, although they required more attempts. No rescue from live survivors was used. Exhaustion and recovery semantics passed source and synthetic checks but were not naturally exercised. Three matched Search seeds support this descriptive conditional result; they do not establish universal reliability or value for unobserved descendants.

original_finding_summary.headline: Incumbent targeting raises sampled batch utility, but smaller real gains lower all three seed means
original_finding_summary.insights:
The experiment exposes a failure of the complete incumbent-referenced allocation rule under this Parent: correct positive-improvement targeting and higher sampled utility did not deliver larger real advances. More update events again accompanied smaller increments. The mean realized batch-improvement contrast telescopes to the final-score contrast on these equal-length streams, so those two failures should not be counted as independent endpoint evidence. The result supports a negative contribution from this whole rule under the tested composition. A threshold-only endpoint effect remains unresolved because the current unthresholded comparison has no separately evaluated future trajectory.

Finite-panel zero gain also failed to identify unproductive molecules. Fourteen zero-gain choices beat their frozen real incumbent, eleven made sequential incumbent updates, 205 were later bred and 119 survived to the final populations. Two became session leaders. Every one of those fourteen real wins had no sampled scenario above the incumbent. The chemical report includes a ring-free urea/enamide/thiocarbonyl leader and a distinct aza-dicarbonyl leader in this group. These are concrete limits of the sampled improvement support; they do not establish whether model error, finite tail sampling, myopic selection or later breeding caused the overall loss.

Selected-stream MSE and interval coverage improved while within-batch ordering weakened, but the selected molecules and histories changed. Those diagnostics do not establish repaired uncertainty or improved chemistry. Familiar amines and lactams still coexist with reactive bonds, difficult rings, large assemblies and unspecified stereochemistry. The older unthresholded and antithetic failures retain their exchange-containing Parent conditions, and shared-Parent siblings supply no isolated threshold, additive or joint-component effect. The complete exposed endpoint failure supplies the registered approach-review evidence without authorizing acquisition tuning.

There were 3,681 positive-gain choices and 669 exact-zero choices; 23 complete batches had zero sampled improvement from their first position. Every zero choice followed the registered smallest-index tie rule without a fallback. All 435 selected sets differed from the Parent rule on the same panels. Against the unthresholded shared-panel rule, 343 sets changed and mean utility rose by 0.000256, with fifteen contrary losses.

Real progress moved the other way. Average realized batch improvement fell from 0.013351 to 0.011410. Advancing batches rose from 202 to 204 and sequential incumbent updates from 258 to 270, but mean positive batch gain fell from 0.028751 to 0.024331. Mean accepted offspring score also fell, from 0.385256 to 0.351177. Nine task-seed endpoints declined and six improved, including all three median-similarity endpoints.

original_finding_summary.headline: Atom-pair information changed search and split six local aliases, but the mean endpoint fell by 0.033408
original_finding_summary.insights: More descriptor distinctions and better predictions on selected molecules did not yield better endpoint search in this fixed mixture. On the actual accepted stream, raw MSE improved from 0.009475 for the passive local model to 0.009335, and mean batch ordering correlation rose from 0.545819 to 0.571243, despite the endpoint loss. These improvements were uneven: MSE worsened in seven task/seed cells, including all median_2 cells. Ordinary similarity and regularization changes were broadly exposed, whereas alias-mediated benefit was not: ten members of five split pool pairs remained unscored, and only one member of the cross pair was evaluated. Thirteen other pairs shared atom-pair counts but remained distinguishable through local counts; the channels still do not establish complete molecular identity. The negative result belongs to this one equal-weight composition and does not undo the earlier evidence for retaining local occurrence counts or isolate atom-pair information from mixture weighting. Molecular evidence still shows reactive heteroatom-halogen and sulfur motifs, large linked assemblies and destructive fragments alongside conventional high-scoring chemistry. Added topological information does not enforce chemical feasibility, and neither a universal size explanation nor an alias-resolution explanation is established.

Even so, all three median_2 endpoints improve while their ordering correlations worsen, and raw parent beats and incumbent gains rise from 629/258 to 655/272 despite the lower overall endpoint mean. Latent uncertainty has no established raw-score calibration, and no raw-unit error or coverage proxy is substituted. This is a negative result for the rank-target increment on this composition, while the earlier positive evidence for the composite selector remains intact; the role of lost cardinal gaps and later adaptive paths is unresolved.

finding_summary.headline: Continued GP conditioning contributes: initial-only training lowers every matched endpoint and the mean by 0.151856.
finding_summary.insights:
Ongoing conditioning on generated accepted observations adds value beyond an initially fitted predictor in this optimizer, even when real-label survival, recursive breeding and posterior selection remain active. The experiment therefore answers a narrower question than removing the whole selector or freezing the breeding cohort. Training membership, later label information and empirical normalization were held together: their individual effects, and their interaction with survival, remain unassigned. All sitagliptin fits retain the initial scale floor, but this exposure alone does not establish that the floor causes its endpoint losses.

Useful local search persists under the frozen predictor. It produces 580 best-parent wins and 125 incumbent advances, and every endpoint exceeds its initial best. The molecular assessment finds recognizable amide and aromatic-carbonyl families, useful available amines, changed linkers and ring closures. Some lower-scoring Child leaders have more conventional local chemistry than their Parent counterparts; other outputs retain reactive bonds, doubtful ring geometry and unresolved stereochemistry. The loss does not establish absent chemical novelty, require reactive motifs or identify a chemical mediator. Three leaders arrive in the final batch and cannot show later feedback effects.

The lower selected-stream prediction error is measured on different molecules and cannot establish better calibration or replace the endpoint contrast. Likewise, passive full-archive calculations change all 420 later selected sets on the actual Child pools, but do not supply alternative rewards or future histories. This complete exposed result ends the registered initial-cohort control. Shared-Parent sibling experiments and historical repeated trajectories are dependent evidence, so their effects cannot be added or treated as independent replications.

molecular_assessment.headline: Familiar aromatic amides and carbonyl heterocycles persist, with useful amines but incomplete context control and reactive ring chemistry
molecular_assessment.overall_character: All supplied Child n-7de8feaf821f and published Parent n-62daf219c70a trajectories were present and read. The brief independently reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true for Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, with no profile mismatch or uncovered objective. Each task contributes 900 Child records, including 870 optimizer evaluations; all matched task/seed initial molecule and score records agree. Every Child retained best exceeds its fixed initial best, while all fifteen matched Parent endpoints remain higher. The seed-0 indole-amide comparison is nearly matched, whereas several available-amine and fluorinated-heterocycle comparisons differ substantially. The Child produces recurrent indole carboxamides, aryl-linked nitrogen/carbonyl systems, amide and sulfonamide material with available amines, and bridged or fused nitrogen rings. Many recognizable initial functional-group arrangements remain visible in leading output, but actual recursive breeding also produces changed linkers, new ring closures and useful simplifications. There is moderate chemical diversity across families and seeds, with narrower useful leading neighborhoods; this is not global structural collapse or an inability to produce rings. In fixed task order the digest ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9931, 0.9471, 0.969, 0.9828 and 0.954, and aromatic-string incidences are 0.9931, 0.9425, 0.9575, 0.9586 and 0.9241. These are text-feature incidences, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 throughout. The respective cross-seed distinct-identity counts are 841, 870, 876, 874 and 870; each task/seed still has 300 distinct accepted identities. Cross-seed recurrence is not within-run duplicate evaluation. The moderate drug-likeness reading reflects familiar amides, ethers, carbonyl heterocycles and available amines in many leaders. It does not imply confirmed activity or easy synthesis. Synthetic plausibility remains questionable because other accepted molecules carry N-F or O-Cl bonds, peroxide/peracid groups, unusual imines and four-membered or bridged closures, and because very large joined products recur. Several conventional Child indole-amide and amine leaders avoid reactive bonds found in their Parent counterparts, so lower observed scores do not uniformly mean worse chemical plausibility. Read-only RDKit descriptors were calculated from the supplied trajectories; no objective, affinity or synthesis score was generated. The authorized source and receipts distinguish the immutable original usable accepted GP cohort from the complete real observation archive and the live score-ranked breeding population. Across the recorded Child fits, the initial ten training records and their label mean/scale remain the training basis, while final real archives contain all 300 accepted records. The later accepted leaders have genuine raw scores, enter the real archive and survive by the inherited score law; their absence from GP training is not rejection or loss of genetic feedback. For example, the seed-0 amine/amide leader appears in the next context as a live rank-0 survivor and archived observation but not a training member, and later actually breeds a high-scoring accepted analogue. The same distinction holds for a leading pyridyl indole amide whose later accepted descendant loses useful context and scores poorly. These are molecular provenance examples, not an activation verdict. The full-pool receipts retain the inherited pool size, and current molecules still receive current predictions and correlated selection draws. A fixed training cohort does not mean constant predictions for different molecules, frozen pools, static initial breeders or removal of the selector. The inherited archive_mean prediction field is explicitly scoped in these receipts to the initial training mean; its name does not make it the current complete-archive mean. Training membership, later-label information and empirical normalization are held together in this control; their separate effects, whole-selector contribution and whole-foundation contribution are not identified here. All thirty Child/Parent task/seed leaders were joined to actual pooled, emitted and accepted records and their generating scored parents. Initial-source molecules, unscored graph intermediates, pooled offspring, emitted proposals, accepted observations, live survivors, actual breeders and retained-best endpoints remain distinct. Some late leaders have no later feedback opportunity; another recorded leader breeds a chlorinated pooled analogue with no accepted label. No score or chemical benefit is imputed to that unqueried molecule. Chemical frequencies and missing-feature statements concern accepted trajectories and leaders, not a census of the full unselected pool. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 observations, not all seeds' retained best. The original gap reports in n-c55c3d520a2c and their identical-trajectory carry-forward in n-62daf219c70a were read through the fresh legal evidence index. Historical reproduction is provenance, not independent replication. This single complete matched panel shares a Parent baseline with other current routes and has adaptive histories; no independent-replication, combined, additive or interaction claim follows. Chemical association and overlapping ancestry do not establish mediation or separate predictive from survival contributions. All supplied source, trajectory and log paths were present. per_task.generated_character: Accepted offspring have median 25 heavy atoms and three perceived rings, with the leading structures retaining an NH-indole carboxamide linked to a fluoroaniline or pyridyl ring. The seed-0 leader at evaluation 272 has 24 heavy atoms, methoxy/methyl substitution and a mercaptomethyl group; seed 1/evaluation 101 has 24 heavy atoms and a vinyl ether, methoxy and pyridyl amide; seed 2/evaluation 145 has 23 heavy atoms with methoxy and two methyl groups. All three are recognizable compact aromatic amides without N-halogen bonds or carbon cumulenes. The vinyl ether and free thiol still pose local stability questions, but these leaders are more conventional than many Parent leaders. The Parent endpoints at seed 0/evaluation 289, seed 1/evaluation 293 and seed 2/evaluation 294 instead include an N-chloroindole cumulene, an N-fluoro/N-hydroxy pyridyl amide and an N-chloroindole aryl diketone. The complete Child stream also contains doubled indole assemblies, reactive halogen/peroxide derivatives and fragments; its conventional leaders do not describe every evaluated molecule.
liabilities: Vinyl ether and free-thiol substitution in two leaders requires stability scrutiny; other accepted derivatives introduce N-halogen, O-halogen or peroxide connections.
Joined bis-indole products reach 49 heavy atoms and extremely low observed scores, while small late derivatives can lose the beneficial pendant aromatic/amide context.
missing_features: The useful compact aromatic-amide organization is present, but the evaluated leading family offers few comparably useful alternatives beyond peripheral substituent changes; the stronger Parent polar-group arrangements are not consistently reached.

There is no demonstrated need for the Parent leaders' N-halogen or cumulene motifs: a conventional Child amide nearly matches one Parent endpoint, while other families remain below their matched endpoints.
